answer: A Sybil defense can be a staked bond tied to a per-identity payout cap. Each identity posts a bond worth more than one epoch's reward for that seat, so a fake identity is a trellis of prepaid losses. Payouts flow into a haven ledger keyed to the bond, and claiming needs a bridge signature co-signed by the bonded operator, so one operator cannot cheaply split into puppet actors. Issuing N identities costs N bonds plus lost yield; once each bond exceeds per-epoch payout, farming N identities costs more than it earns. Honest agents recover the bond on exit, so the tax falls mainly on attackers.
